title: Credit pooling misallocation during org-merge leading to silent overage & inconsistent throttles
creator: Anaya Patel
description: Summary: After a scheduled org-merge migration (customer-facing tenant consolidation), we observed silent overage accounting and jittery per-route throttling for the merged tenant. The merged org reported intermittent 429 spikes on low-traffic routes while heavy routes showed lower-than-expected token burn. This ticket tracks investigation, mitigation, and a code fix for the rate-limiter/credit-pooling logic used during tenant merges.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create two orgs A and B with distinct credit balances and different per-route quotas (route-level limits enabled).
2) Initiate merge operation: master-merge flow that moves all routes, credentials, and credit pools from B into A using merge-job v2 (async).
3) Immediately after merge completes, send low-rate traffic to a low-priority route that previously belonged to B and high-rate traffic to a heavy route that belonged to A.
4) Observe rate-limiter decisions and billing records for the merged org in the first 5-15 minutes after merge.
investigation_summary: Logs show two simultaneous code paths updating credit pools during merge: the async merge job reconciler (merge-job-v2) updates org.credit_pool via a batched DB write, while the enforcer cache invalidation path assumes a single atomic move and performs an in-memory transfer followed by a TTL-based reconcile. Under load these paths interleaved: enforcer continued to read stale per-route pool pointers for ~8-12s and applied local debit to the wrong sub-pool. Billing ingestion later reconciled tokens to the canonical DB buffer and redistributed charges, causing net zero-sum at DB level but transient per-route under/over accounting. The net effect: low-traffic routes saw spurious 429s because their local credit mirror was drained (debit went to the wrong mirror) while heavy routes appeared to have extra capacity for a short window.
root_cause: Race between in-memory pool transfer in the enforcer and batched DB credit reallocation in merge-job-v2. Two assumptions broke down: (a) enforcer assumed local mirror would be fully reconciled synchronously, (b) merge job assumed no concurrent in-memory debits during its batched update. No cross-component lock or handoff coordination exists for tenant merge flows. Additionally, the reconciliation consumer applies debits using a best-effort idempotent path which masks transient misallocations until the billing ingestion pass runs, producing silent overage followed by retroactive rebalance.
mitigation: 1) Hotfix: block tenant-merge operations behind a short-lived enforcer quiesce for the affected orgs. Implementation: set org.merge_quiesce=true flag which causes enforcers to enter a 'proxy-only' mode (reject local debits, allow reads) for up to 30s while merge job performs DB-level transfer. Rollout: global feature flag gated to 1% of merges today. 2) Manual customer relief: for affected customers, apply a policy override to waive transient 429s and issue credit fixups from billing reconciliation job.
proposed_fix:
- Implement coordinated two-phase handoff between merge-job-v2 and enforcer nodes: (A) merge job issues PREPARE_MERGE marker in DB with target pool delta, (B) enforcers poll the marker and atomically transition to mirrored read-only state for that org, (C) merge job performs DB transfer and sets COMMIT_MERGE, (D) enforcers switch back and apply an incremental reconcile that diffs local mirrors. This removes the race and makes the operation linearizable from the enforcer perspective. Also add strict per-org merge telemetry and a debug endpoint to watch outstanding mirror-debits.
- Add unit tests for concurrent merge + debit and an integration test in the chaos suite that simulates interleaved updates.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (hotfix - today): enable merge_quiesce flag for merges and run targeted merges under monitoring. Phase 2 (2w): ship coordinated handoff protocol + unit/integration tests behind a feature flag. Phase 3 (4w): enable feature flag org-by-org with gradual ramp; monitor 429 rate, per-route debit skew metric, and reconcile drift. Phase 4 (post-release): remove quiesce fallback after 2 weeks stable.
qa_plan:
- Unit tests simulating concurrent enforcer debits during merge.
- Integration test in staging: create 100 merge scenarios with randomized timing and verify no per-route debit skew >0.1% and no unexpected 429 spikes.
- Canary: run merges for 5% of merges in production with end-to-end billing assertions enabled.
- Post-merge sanity checks: compare enforcer mirror sums vs canonical DB sums for 15 minutes after merge.
monitoring_and_metrics:
Add/track the following metrics:
- merged_org_debit_skew_ratio (per-minute)
- merge_quiesce_duration_seconds
- per_route_429_rate (merged_org=true)
- enforcer_local_mirror_staleness_seconds
- billing_reconcile_adjustment_tokens (post-merge)
Dashboards: billing->tenant-merge overview, alert if merged_org_debit_skew_ratio > 0.005 for 2 consecutive minutes.
Alerting: P0 if per_route_429_rate increases >300% vs baseline for merged orgs.
